incidents.summary:
Russia struck two major bridges in Kyiv while Ukraine hit Moscow's link to annexed Crimea for a second consecutive night, with the exchanges occurring ahead of Xi-Trump-Putin talks. Jared Kushner described a U.S. plan for postwar Ukraine centered on security guarantees, the prospect of EU accession, and a comprehensive economic recovery program. Meanwhile, Russia pressed a bombing campaign intended to deprive Kyiv and other cities of heat, running water, and sanitation this winter even as peace talks continue.
President Trump said Vladimir Putin is "backing down a bit" on Ukraine while adding that he "could have been much tougher," remarks made as leaders prepare for a round of meetings. Reporting also describes Trump reversing course on Ukraine ahead of talks with Putin and Xi in China, with European leaders organizing a parallel summit in Berlin to press for a seat at the table. Separately, Russian lawmakers are moving to raise penalties for war-related offences, and commentary weighs whether trading the Donbas for NATO membership could deliver Ukraine ironclad security guarantees.

Ukraine struck additional warehouses of Russia's top online retailer Wildberries and intensified attacks on Ozon, causing economic disruption. In leadership moves, President Zelensky replaced the commander-in-chief with Mykhailo Drapatyi and fired Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, sparking protests. Meanwhile, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Russia's Lavrov in Manila, expressing readiness to help end the war but noting no quick deal is imminent.
Ukrainian strikes on Russia's Wildberries warehouses produced massive pillars of black smoke as fires raged at the facilities. Russia, stretched by Ukraine's drone attacks on its Black Sea Fleet, has pulled all warships from the Mediterranean Sea. Both sides have increased bridge strikes to disrupt resupply networks, indicating expectations of a prolonged stalemate, while the Kremlin warned against optimism on peace following the Rubio-Lavrov meeting.
The EU passed its 21st sanctions package with 218 new designations targeting Russia, including vessels that refuel shadow fleet tankers. Ukrainian strikes continued to hit Russian Wildberries warehouses, while new airstrikes caused deaths in both Ukraine and Russia, and a drone was shot down over NATO airspace.

There have been no immediate reports of injuries or damage resulting from the earthquake. The USGS stated that the earthquake occurred 43 kilometers south of the coastal town of Puerto San Jose, at a depth of 35 kilometers. The tremor was also felt by residents in El Salvador and Nicaragua; both countries indicated that there is no risk of a tsunami. On September 16, a 5.3-magnitude earthquake struck southern Guatemala.
